text: Before the tables, the warehouse they live in: Redshift Serverless, workgroup northfield-analytics, namespace northfield-dw, database northfielddw, base capacity 8 RPUs. The tables themselves live under a schema called analytics: one fact table, fact_orders, and three dimension tables.

This is a deliberately small star schema. dim_product, dim_customer, and dim_date each hold descriptive attributes Finance and Ops will filter and group by. Region stays directly on the fact table, since it's a flat attribute with nothing further to normalize out. fact_orders itself sits at the same order-line grain the curated Parquet already uses.

Two settings on fact_orders do real work. DISTSTYLE KEY with DISTKEY on customer_id means every order row for a given customer lands on the same compute slice as that customer's dimension row, so the join both planned reports run routinely happens locally instead of shuffling data across the cluster.

SORTKEY on dt matches exactly how Finance and Ops actually ask for data: show me last month, show me the last seven days. With rows physically ordered by date, a date-range filter only scans the blocks that overlap that range, skipping the rest of the table's history entirely.

And the warehouse itself runs Serverless specifically because Northfield's query load spikes around month-end and goes quiet otherwise, which per-RPU-second billing fits far better than an always-on cluster. Next lesson: actually getting the curated Parquet into these tables with a real COPY command.
